title: The bulk reactivation confirmation shows its two lines
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create two inactive parts for this test, part A and part B.
  • Give parts A and B part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists both.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Inactive tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type the shared start of the part numbers in the Search box.
  2. Click the three-dot actions button (⋮) in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  3. Click Activate parts.
  4. Click the part A row.
  5. Click the part B row.
  6. Click Activate on the dark bar.
  7. Click Cancel in the confirmation.
  8. Click the part B row.
  9. Click Activate on the dark bar.
  10. Click Cancel in the confirmation.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Parts A and B are listed.

Step 2:

  • The menu opens.

Step 3:

  • Bulk mode turns on.

Step 4:

  • The bar reads 1 selected.

Step 5:

  • The bar reads 2 selected.

Step 6:

  • The confirmation reads "Activate parts?", "2 parts selected.", then "These parts can be added to new work again." and "Existing records that use them stay as they are."
  • There is no "Stock, cost of goods" line.

Step 7:

  • The confirmation closes.

Step 8:

  • The bar reads 1 selected.

Step 9:

  • It reads "1 part selected.", then "This part can be added to new work again." and "Existing records that use it stay as they are."

Step 10:

  • The confirmation closes and nothing changed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S10-R8: “For a reactivation from the bulk bar, the confirmation states "These parts can be added to new work again." ("This part ..." for one), followed by "Existing records that use them stay as they are." ("... that use it ..." for one).”
